out_of_hospital_midwife.kit_ordering: Midwives must become approved Texas NSHS submitters; order newborn screening blood spot cards and supplies through the DSHS Newborn Screening Lab (Submitter ID request form required).
out_of_hospital_midwife.submission_deadline: First screen ideally 24-48 hours of age; second screen at 7-14 days (minimum 168 hours).
out_of_hospital_midwife.specimen_tracking: Submitter tracks results via the DSHS Newborn Screening Lab portal / submitter account.

metabolic_screening.opt_out_form_number: Newborn Screen Blood Test Refusal Form (English; Spanish: Newborn Screen Blood Test Refusal Form Final_202406.pdf)
metabolic_screening.state_form_note: Texas provides an official state Blood Test Refusal Form. Texas Health & Safety Code Ch. 33 mandates screening; 25 Tex. Admin. Code Â§ 97.136 requires prophylactic eye treatment but a parent, managing conservator, or guardian may object. A signed refusal is filed with the provider/medical record.
metabolic_screening.statute: Texas Health & Safety Code Â§ 33.001 et seq. (Newborn Screening); 25 Tex. Admin. Code Â§ 97.136 (eye prophylaxis objection)

hearing_screening.program_name: Texas Early Hearing Detection and Intervention (TEHDI)
hearing_screening.out_of_hospital_path: In community/home birth, the midwife must provide TEHDI education materials, review all three universal screens (blood spot, hearing, CCHD), and document any hearing-screen refusal in the client's medical chart (state's official Newborn Screen Blood Test Refusal Form may be used).
hearing_screening.statute: Texas Health & Safety Code Â§ 33.011 (hearing screening); 1-3-6 EHDI benchmarks

cchd_screening.out_of_hospital_performer: Attending midwife or physician in the community birth setting performs pulse oximetry (CCHD) and documents it; refusal documented in the medical chart.
cchd_screening.statute: Texas Health & Safety Code Â§ 33.011 (critical congenital heart defect screening)

erythromycin_eye_ointment.waiver: Parental/guardian objection allowed; provider commits no offense if administration is refused. Hospital typically requires a signed refusal waiver.
erythromycin_eye_ointment.note: 0.5% erythromycin ointment applied within two hours of birth by physician, nurse, or midwife.

vitamin_k.note: Texas does not mandate vitamin K; parental choice of oral, intramuscular shot, or decline. Documented in the birth record.

hepatitis_b_vaccine.note: Birth dose reported to ImmTrac2 by the birthing facility/hospital; infants born to HBsAg-positive mothers receive HBIG + vaccine within 12 hours and are reported for case management.

gestational_diabetes.midwife_role: Licensed midwives in Texas screen for and counsel on gestational diabetes as part of prenatal care; abnormal glucose screening is referred for diagnostic testing (provider-to-provider referral).
gestational_diabetes.note: Prenatal informed-choice item; no state newborn-screening form. Managed in prenatal care, not via the NBS program.

group_b_strep.midwife_role: Licensed midwives offer GBS screening (culturing) in late pregnancy and administer or arrange intrapartum prophylaxis per protocol for out-of-hospital births when indicated.
group_b_strep.note: Prenatal informed-choice item; no state newborn-screening form.
